You say that: "The terrorists were controlling that area." And then a little further down in paragraph 35 you say that: "Prilep was the furthest point reached." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, because the terrorists were defending the Radonjic Lake, they concentrated there around the hazelnut farm and around the school, and then they set out towards Dasinovac and that whole area up to Jablanica was held by them so the MUP could no longer enter that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear, those were the only two attempts made by the MUP to enter the territory east of the main road at any time between the 24th of March and September; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: My evidence is that on those two occasions there were organised attempts to enter because there was operative information that people had been kidnapped and killed in the Radonjic Lake area. There were operations from time to time, but it was not possible to penetrate into the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I just want to be absolutely crystal clear about this, Mr. Zlatkovic. You agree that in paragraph 28 of your statement: "It is true," you say, "that the police never returned to Gllogjan between the 24th of March and September." Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It's correct, yes. They only established roads so that the population from Pec towards Decani, Djakovica, Prizren, and so on could get supplies. But on both sides there were terrorist groups, well-organised groups, so that nobody could use those roads because the Albanians were informed through their media that they couldn't move along the roads at such and such a time --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- people knew that and didn't move. Some Serbs --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me, Mr. Zlatkovic. I don't need a lengthy explanation from you. I just need confirmation from you --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I just need confirmation from you that your testimony before the Trial Chamber is, first of all, that the MUP never entered Gllogjan between March and September, and you've agreed that that is the case; yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it could not enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And your testimony is also that during the 9th of August operation the MUP could not get any further east than Prilep, which is on the main road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct, because if the MUP had come to Radonjic Lake, we would have found those victims in August, not in September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like, if you would, please, to ask you to look at -- you should have a brown folder. You haven't got it. I'll ask that it be handed to you. If you could turn, please, to tab 35 in that folder. Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, this is annex 10 to Mr. Zlatkovic's witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we just be clear, Mr. Zlatkovic, that this is a document you, yourself, wrote, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is in the form of a report delivered to the district public prosecutor in Pec along with the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And in this report you record a significant number of what you say are attacks by the KLA on Serb MUP patrols, don't you, amongst other things?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to just look at some of those with you, if I may, for a moment or two. Now, the first one I want -- and I'm going to go through them as far as I can in chronological order. I think you can confirm, can you, please, that the entries in your record here are not, in fact, in chronological order. They jump about in time a little.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the first -- the first entry I want to ask you about is in the English translation at page 8, and for you, if you look at the numbers in the top right-hand corner of the B/C/S version, can you see that there is a number beginning U0167, do you see that, at the top right-hand corner of each page? Do you see that number beginning --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: 0167, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, what I -- that is, in fact, the page I want to ask you to look at but if you can concentrate on the last three digits, I'm going to take you to a number of pages. And if you just look at the last three digits at the top right-hand corner, we're looking now at the one that ends 573, and that's an entry which bears a reference of KU 196/98. Do you have that one? Do you see that? It's the second full paragraph on 573, Mr. Zlatkovic. Are you on page 573? Do you see the second full entry? Each of them has a separate serial number --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. 196 through 198, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one. I want you to remind yourself about the format of this document because we're going to need to go through quite a number of those entries, and I would like you to start with that one, please. Does that record that on the 9th of August, at about 7.30 in the evening in the Biteska Cuka sector, Gjakove municipality, an ethnic Albanian DTG carried out a terrorist attack, firing at members of the Serbian MUP. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us where is the Biteska Cuka sector?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Biteska Cuka is above Babaloc, between the villages of Babaloca, Glodjane, Savara [phoen] and Erec?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's just be clear: There were two large hills between Lake Radoniq and the main road. There's Erecka Suka which is next to the village of Babaloc?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there's -- and there is Suka Bitesh which is immediately on the banks of the lake, on the western side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Above Babaloc itself and it stretches towards Lake Radonjic, it stretches in the direction of Lake Radonjic. But Radonjic Lake is on the left-hand side. Lake Radonjic touches on Biteska Cuka and the bodies were found at the entrance to the canal, that's when we look towards the east on the left-hand side, that's where the corpses were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. Lake Radoniq is immediately adjacent to Biteska Cuka, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does it follow from this entry that on the 9th of August there was a Serbian MUP unit in the Suka Bitesh sector?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible. I wasn't there at the time, but it's possible, yes, because preparations were carried out for the final assault against the terrorists, and to get to Lake Radonjic at any cost because there was information that there were corpses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see, but you've told us just a few moments ago that on the 9th of August the MUP did not manage to penetrate any further east of the main road than Prilep. That was your evidence just a few moments ago. It's not true, is it, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: The truth is that from Prilep you couldn't enter; that's the truth. But we reached Biteska Cuka with the fighting because Stojan was a wounded policeman and several other policemen were wounded, so one unit reached Biteska Cuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one unit?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that unit, the one where the man was wounded. Perhaps there was another unit that arrived. I don't know. I wasn't there. I just conducted an on-site investigation where the people had been killed and gathered the necessary information to file criminal reports, operational information I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you conducted an on-site --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when was that done?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: After the fighting had stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And when was that? How long after the incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: As soon as it was reported. The team from Djakovica set out straight away for the location. We couldn't find the man there because he'd been transported to hospital straight away and he's an invalid to this day. He comes from the region I come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you managed to get there on the same day, did you, the 9th of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just exactly where was it that this incident had happened in relation to Suka Bitesh?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Behind Biteska Cuka is the village of Erec. Now, how far it is, how many kilometres, I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just help us, was it in the village of Erec that this alleged attack took place?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: The police prepared its units to launch an assault on the terrorist groups, and it set out in the early hours of the morning. The first incident took place in Erec village when the terrorist group attacked the police that was moving along the Djakovica-Decani road, and that's where they started out from.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you help me for a moment, please, by looking at entry KU 220, which you will find --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For Your Honours, it is page 10 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for you, Mr. Zlatkovic, it is page 574. And you'll find it -- you'll find it just about -- just below halfway down page 574.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: KU, what did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: KU 220/98. Do you have that one?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does that record that on the same day, on the 9th of August, an ethnic Albanian DTG carried out a terrorist attack on members of the Serbian MUP who were carrying out regular assignments near Gllogjan [sic] village, Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes. "In this terrorist attack Slobodan Veljkovic, Pristina policeman, sustained a injury."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What does the word "regular assignments" when you use it in this report, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: In this report, when the term "regular assignments" is used, regular assignments of the police force mean to maintain law and order and to patrol the area and uncover the perpetrators of crimes. At this point in time the perpetrators of the crimes were terrorists because they had kidnapped people previously and killed people and mistreated people, and so on and so forth. So it was the task of the police to find them and to arrest them, and if they put up resistance then quite obviously the police would retaliate in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it was a regular patrol in the area near to Gllogjan; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: A regular unit set out from Djakovica with the intention of liberating the road, and then they divided up into different patrols and that's how the conflict and clash came about.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could just, whilst we're on the same -- in the same approximate area, if we could look at page 578 for you and page 6 in the English translation -- I'm sorry, I do apologise, page 15 in the English translation. Do you see an entry that reads KU 406?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, 406/98, the 9th of August, 1998, at around 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So does it appear from that entry that there was a MUP patrol in Dujak on the 9th of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in all villages. It blocked off all the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, what blocked off all the villages?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: The members of the police force, and I said at the beginning that the communication route between Pec, the road between Pec, Decani, and Djakovica had been taken over for months. Now, in addition to the fact that the road had been taken control of, many people had also been kidnapped, a lot of people had been kidnapped. So the police decided to settle accounts with the terrorists and uncover the perpetrators and free the people who had been kidnapped. So that's why they set out in organised fashion and the units were divided up into patrols and other smaller units, whatever you like to call them --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- squads, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- But there was shooting from all these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you look at the following entry, please, 430/98. Does that indicate that on the 10th of August there was a MUP patrol in the village of Bitesh?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And there were two Biteshes, both very close to one another. Donji Bites and then there's a very small village called Gornji Bites. Which Bites would this be a reference to in your document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: In this document it is Donji Bites.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Donji Bites is immediately on the banks of Lake Radoniq, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Gornji Bites is on the banks of Lake Radonjic, whereas Donji Bites is near Biteska Cuka, above this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zlatkovic, we --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- Above this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, we all have maps in this case in this courtroom and I'm not going to take time showing you a map, but I suggest to you that Donji Bites is immediately to the western side of Lake Radoniq and, indeed, the closest village to the shores of Lake Radoniq on its western side. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly, possibly. I spent there a year and a half -- well, you can see it from the map and I'll point out where it happened, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why did you say in your witness statement at paragraph 34 that during the operation on the 9th of August, the MUP did not go to the Lake Radoniq area, Mr. Zlatkovic, why did you say that in your witness statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said it because you couldn't reach Lake Radonjic because it was fiercely defended. Lake Radonjic was fiercely defended.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were Serbian forces stationed on Suka Bitesh, the hill immediately to the west of Lake Radoniq and overlooking Bitesh village, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but do you know how far the distance is from that point to the site where the dead people were found?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking about dead people; I'm asking about your witness statement, Mr. Zlatkovic, where you categorically state that: On the 9th of August operation, the MUP did not go to the Lake Radoniq area and did not enter any further than Prilep, and it's not true, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: That is true, but you're trying to mislead me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No I'm not. You're, with respect, trying to mislead us, with respect --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- trying to confuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not at all --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm speaking very sincerely, most sincerely. I don't wish to add anything because I've taken the solemn declaration not to add anything or to subtract anything, but just to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, could you -- since that is your approach, Mr. Zlatkovic, could you turn to page 574 in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, this is page 8 of the English translation -- I'm sorry, page 9 of the English translation. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 574, yes, thank you, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you have an entry that reads 217 on that page?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: 217, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does that tell you that on the 11th of August there is a reported attack by the KLA? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, near the village of Glodjane, Decani municipality, and serious life-threatening injuries were sustained, et cetera, and Djuro Vabros of the Novi Sad SAJ was injured. Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that says -- you are there recording the presence of SAJ, anti-terrorist forces in and around the area of Gllogjan on the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were deployed then. They weren't deployed when the first attack came and when Otovic was killed, but otherwise they were deployed because they are, indeed, anti-terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there they were in the area around Gllogjan; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: No. The shooting came from Glodjane. It says at 07 hours, members -- on the 11th of August, 1998, at 0700 hours, members of the DTG of ethnic Albanian DTG carried out a terrorist attack firing a mortar on members of the Serbian MUP who were carrying out their regular duties and assignments near Glodjane village, Decani municipality. In this terrorist attack, a serious life-threatening injuries were sustained by Mile Nikolic, member of the Novi Sad SAJ, while Djuro Vabros, member of the Novi Sad SAJ was seriously injured, which means that a mine had been launched from a mortar. You know that Decani Glodjane is not a long way away from each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are you suggesting that this incident took place in Decani?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, not in Decani. No, it wasn't in Decani. It was from the Glodjane direction that the mine was launched. Now, whether they were 500 metres away from the road leading to Glodjane or whether they were on the road itself, on the communication route, I can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the following entry, Mr. Zlatkovic, records a further incident that day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm mainly interested in where the targeted people were. Could you please explore that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because that's not entirely clear to me at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you help us with that, please, Mr. Zlatkovic. The entry you've just been looking at refers to members of the Serbian MUP who were carrying out regular duties and assignments near Glodjane village. Do you see that? Where were --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where were they, these SAJ officers, when the attack occurred on the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a mixed unit, and they set up check-points along the road, to ensure free passage of traffic along the road. There were points at Prilep at the beginning of the village and check-points in Rastavica as well and by the roadside in Drenovac and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You make it very clear in these entries when you're talking about Prilep and Drenovac and Carrabreg where specifically were these SAJ members you've recorded being on patrol near Gllogjan? When they were attacked, where were they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: They were there, by the road --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness answered that question. He said they were -- after he said it was a mixed unit, that they were -- "they set up check-points along the road." I understood that answer to be that they were therefore along the road setting up check-points to ensure free passage, and I understood the reference to Gllogjan as on the road near to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: More in the direction of Decan or Djakovica. That's how I understood the answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I be absolutely clear that we've understood your testimony correct. Are you saying that this incident occurred on the main road?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. This is how it was: The main road -- well, as what happened happened on the 9th of August, the units of Mr. Ramush Haradinaj and the rest withdrew deeper towards Lake Radonjic, towards Lake Radonjic. The Visnjarnik area or the cherry orchards or whatever and towards Jablanica. Now, the police, at 100 or 200 metres in front of the mosque, I remember that they set up a police check-point in front of the mosque in Prilep and there was another check-point 2 or 300 metres away from the road. Now, from up there they shot and probably the mine fell there, and the truth of it was that people were wounded. Now, whether this was done by this one or that one, I really don't know. But there were Ramush's forces there, in that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And -- and if we could just look at page 573 for a moment in your report, which for us is on page 9 in the English again. At 205 -- do you have the entry KU 205, where you describe an incident taking place in Gramaqel? What does the reference to Gramaqel village mean there on the 10th of August, this is KU --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just take a minute to find it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: KU 205, which you'll find at page 573 in your version.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And that refers, does it not, to an incident that took place in Gramaqel village?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you help us with that, was that an incident also that took place along the main road but somewhere near to Gramaqel or was that in the village itself?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: That was also the road leading towards Dubrava, Babaloc, Gramocelj -- it was all in the same operation, that same action. There was an action underway, and that's when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me see if I've understood your evidence correctly, but there are aspects of it that I'm finding a little difficult to follow. Is it your evidence that there were forces that penetrated into Gramaqel this operation? As far as Gramaqel --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As far as Dubrava, yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As far as Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the entrance to Glodjane and the terrorist group withdrew to where I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as far as the village of Bitesh?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Bites is to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Dujak as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You see, Mr. Zlatkovic, these incidents that you've recorded as having taken place between the 9th and the 12th of August, these all occurred in the context of a major military offensive involving joint operations between the VJ and the MUP to clear that area of the KLA, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw the police but I didn't see the army so I don't know whether the army took part. Let me repeat again. All I did was to carry out on on-site investigation, not only to see where the Serb forces had been killed or civilians, but the Albanians, too. It was my task to go with the investigative judge, if it was safe for an investigative judge to come in from Pec, it was my task to carry out the on-site investigation and to transform the bodies for a post mortem to be able to see what they had died of, and then to hand over the bodies to their families, if the families came forward; if not, then the procedure was instituted as is customary with dead bodies. So it was my job to carry out an on-site investigation. If there was no investigative judge present, then I had to go on to the locality with an escort, of course, and do my job. Now, whether the army took part or not, I don't know. Perhaps it did. Perhaps they took part somewhere over there in the mountains, I don't know. What I saw was the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the investigations you conducted into each of these incidents between the 9th and the 12th of August, is it your evidence that you were not aware that there was a major joint military and MUP operation to sweep through that area and take control of Gllogjan at that time? You didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that there was an operation underway, but I didn't see the army. I saw just one tank, and I say that in my statement. When we arrive for the first time in Glodjane and when we found, or rather, Lake Radonjic by the canal when we found the dead bodies, then a military tank --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, let --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- went in front of the police and it cleared the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you, I apologise for interrupting you, but that is a much later --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- That is a much later part of your account, that deals with what happened in September. I'm asking you about the 9th of August and the period between the 9th and 12th and the question I'm trying to get you to answer, if I may, please, since you investigated each of these incidents did you not become aware in the course of your investigations that there was a major offensive, a Serbian offensive taking place, and that these people were casualties of that offensive?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has already testified that he did not remember that, and the same question is asked again. I can't see how he could answer in a different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Dutertre, this last comment which is not appropriate. Could you please tell us whether you ever became aware during your investigations that it was a major offensive and that the army was involved in it as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't say anything on that score. What I'm telling you is this: Perhaps later on when there was the NATO aggression, perhaps then the army took part, but on this occasion I didn't see the army except once and I said this in my statement, I saw them previously, and I'm sure it says so here and I don't mind standing by that because that is what I said, but that there was some offensive underway, well, I don't know. Possibly, but I didn't see it. I just did not see it. All I know is the police took part, it took part with the weapons that a police force is issued with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You emphasised and you made a clear distinction between what you saw and what you perhaps learned. Now, when you made these investigations, apart from what you saw, did you become aware, in whatever way, at that moment or in these days that the army was involved in the operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was not aware of this. I didn't learn of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I went last -- I apologise for interrupting, but let me say I went last when everything was over. When everything was over, I would come in last to carry out an on-site investigation and I saw the police check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so I understand you were investigating the circumstances in which these people had died, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you just look, please, behind tab 31 in the brown file. Now, if you can look at this document with me, if you will, for a moment. It is an order issued by Colonel Dragan Zivanovic of the 125th Motorised Brigade of the VJ based in Peje dated the 8th of August, and can you see that the objective is described at the top in the following words: "Immediately begin preparations to provide support to MUP forces" -- do you have that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just bear with me. "Immediately begin preparations to provide support to MUP forces fighting DTS in the general area of Glodjane village." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we could just look down here, please, at 2.6 and 2.7. Do you see there there is a reference to: "BG," fighting group, "52 with reinforcements shall support the attack of the main forces of the MUP 2nd Detachment, Pristina CPJP company and SAJ on the axis of Radonjicka Suka to Saptej to Rznic, and with part of its forces shall participate in coordinated action on the axis of Donji Bites to Gramocelj to Saptej." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I see that, but I never had access to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I'm not asking you whether you did. Can you look at 2.7, please. "BG-549 shall support the attack of the MUP 9th Detachment and the Prizren CPJP on the axis of Erec village-Erecka Suma-Babaloc-Rastavica." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us a few minutes ago in the incident that I took you to on the 9th of August in the area around Erecka Suka that you had gone the same day on the 9th of August into that area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you investigate each of these incidents that you've recorded on the 9th, the 10th, and the 11th of August in that area on the same day at around the same time?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd understood your testimony then that you never saw any VJ forces at all in that area at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I still maintain that I never did. Perhaps they carried out that attack earlier on and then left.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Before you got there on the 9th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Because when the fighting is over and the road is safe, that's when I go, unless it's an exceptional case or something is urgent. In this case there was fighting, and then I went there later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Leaving the VJ aside, did you know that there was a coordinated attack involving the MUP, the SAJ, and the PJP to sweep through those villages and take control of them and that that's the context in which these incidents occurred? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see because they've been made in your report, if you forgive me for suggesting it to you, they've been made in your report to appear as though these are unprovoked terrorist attacks on MUP going about their regular patrolling duties, haven't they? That's how you've recorded them in your report. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. That's how I recorded it and that's certainly how it was, because let me tell you this was not a divided territory. At that time the police was still controlling that area and it had to go in to see what was happening. I'm not blaming either of the sides for the incident. One side thought the police shouldn't go in, the other side felt the police should go in. It was up to me to carry out an on-site investigation subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you stick to your evidence that these forces never entered Gllogjan at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what forces are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The MUP, the SAJ, they never entered Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible that they got as far as Mr. Ramush's house. It's possible they were there, but they never got to Lake Radonjic. Because right after that the same thing started up again. They might have got as far as Ramush's house, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You see, I began my cross-examination of you, Mr. Zlatkovic, by asking you about the first sentence in paragraph 28 in your witness statement where you make a categorical assertion that the police never returned to Gllogjan between March and September. Now, what is the position? Do you know the answer to that question one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I know the answer that the police was unable to reach Lake Radonjic from the time Otovic was killed until the time they did get there in September. That's all I know. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just play you a piece of videotape, please, briefly. You'll have to watch the screen for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you are playing from --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm playing from the BBC video, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's tab 23 in the brown file, the transcript is D69.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you provided the transcript to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The transcript is in the brown file at tab 23, which the interpreters have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we are following the usual procedure, that is, one of the interpreters reading and the other interpreter translating on the basis of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "The Serbs know that they have the upper hand and they're determined to press home the advantage. This time it was the village of Glodjane in flames, shelled and machine-gunned into submission. On the other side the KLA allowed us exclusive access to their new front line. They're nervous but determined. Some of these men come from this village. They know what's happened up ahead and that they now lie directly in the path of the Serb offensive which has already removed the rebel fighters from most of their strongholds in Kosovo. The waiting is tense, but already it's clear that they won't have to wait long. The shells are now falling on Rznic. Against artillery, there's little that the KLA has been able to do but run. All this is happening while both sides consider peace proposals and the international community struggles to find a way forward. Despite the international diplomacy, the situation on the ground remains unchanged. The Serbs are still pressing their offensive, the KLA still defending their villages and communities. The Serbs, of course, don't see it that way. They insist that the rebel fighters are the problem, and without them so much misery and destruction could have been avoided. Here it's the paramilitary police that are bearing down on the KLA. In other places we saw heavily armed units of the Army of Yugoslavia. The Serbs say they now regard this as a mopping-up operation. For the KLA it's becoming a battle for survival. When there is fighting, there are, of course, more refugees. Almost 200.000 people have been made homeless by this conflict. The aid agencies have been hoping that they would return to their villages. What's happened today makes that a very distant prospect. Jeremy Cooke, BBC news, Rznic, Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. End it there. Thank you very much. Has the translation caught up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, the Serbian offensive that swept through this area between the 9th and 12th of August took control of Gllogjan and Irzniq and all the area surrounding it, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, could we please know what is meant by "the area surrounding it"?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well, I'll put the question more specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, the Serbian offensive that swept through the area to the east of the main Peje to Gjakove road between the 9th and the 12th of August took control of the villages of Gllogjan and Irzniq, did it not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I think -- well, this is a news report and I see both sides there. And whenever there's fighting, civilians flee. I'm not a politician. I was only a member of the police carrying out on-site investigations. I was not interested in who was right here. The members of the KLA were fighting to have their own government, their own --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- their own authorities which they did not have the right to at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me for interrupting you again. I'm not asking you to express an opinion on the rights and wrongs. I'm asking you to confirm, please, that you know that the Serbian offensive at that time took control of Gllogjan and Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't just the Serbian offensive. Both sides were shooting at each other; that's how it was in my view --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, that is not the core of the question. The core of the question is whether the Serb forces during those -- whether you call them skirmishes or battles or doesn't matter, whether they finally gained control over Irzniq and Gllogjan. That's the question -- or at least went as far as into the village of Irzniq and Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, judging by this footage, most probably they got on to the foot-hills of those villages. I can see that on this footage, and then they set up those check-points in front of the mosque in Prilep or near the school in Rznic or in front of the school, I'm not sure exactly where, and so on. But what I'm saying is they never reached Lake Radonjic. They certainly got to the outskirts of the village because the people withdrew. They saw that there was strong forces, they withdrew towards Jablanica, wherever it was that they went, and they took that area, those people, and set up check-points, but they weren't left there in peace, they were attacked right away either from -- by snipers or from mortars. So there was always sporadic firing, and they kept causing problems for us, for us who were supposed to go out on to the field and carry out on-site investigations because we weren't safe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is all understood. Mr. Emmerson is just testing your statement where you say that since the 24th of March that the police never came back to Gllogjan, whereas it now -- I do understand that your testimony is that in early August they never reached Lake Radonjic, which of course is not exactly the same, but that's how I now understand your testimony. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, they couldn't exercise control in Glodjane, function normally, mount patrols, communicate with the citizens --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, I have to interrupt you. The question simply is -- I'm not asking how long they stayed there, but the question is whether they in this -- well, let's say around the 10th of August, whether the forces went as far as Gllogjan entering the village. I do understand that you say they could not function there normally, that's all understood. But the question is whether they ever reached that village in that period of time, yes or no. And I now, from your emphasis, on that they did not reach Lake Radonjic, I do understand that you are not testifying anymore that they never reached at that moment in time the village of Gllogjan and the village of Irzniq. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have one additional question for you in this context, and that is the following. Mr. Emmerson has put to you a document which describes in some detail as how the MUP, that is police forces, and the VJ would act together at this moment, at this moment in time, that is, around the 10th of August, 1998. Mr. Emmerson also showed you a BBC footage which shows -- well, substantial combat activity. Now, I'd like to again put the question to you whether you never got any clue at this moment in time when you were doing, during a couple of days, your on-site investigations, whether you never got a clue from the presence of the VJ and combined operations in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not get any such clues or indications that the VJ participated. It's possible they did. As this document exists, they certainly did, but I did not see them myself. Well, this document shows that they participated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the images you saw on this BBC footage, is that what you would under normal circumstances be the image you would see if there's a police operation going on, just police operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I saw the KLA there, the police on the footage, and the anti-terrorist unit, those in the grey camouflage uniforms and bandannas on their heads, that was the anti-terrorist unit. The BBC said it was a paramilitary unit. I don't know how they could say that, but both those units participated, the anti-terrorist unit and the police, which was then called the PJP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's time for a break. Could you give us an indication as far as time is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, in real terms I've got two significant areas to touch upon. One is the process of interrogation that took place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and the second is the canal itself. I would have thought I'm likely to have another -- obviously entirely subject to the Trial Chamber's direction another hour, hour and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which would mean that we could not conclude today. We will consider that and if you would please already prepare for speeding up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is not any anticipation of what the Chamber will decide --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I indicate that we are expecting to save some time later in the week with a witness who is currently due to give evidence via videolink and who may well, we anticipate, be able to be reduced to an attestation of a 92 ter statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it 92 ter or --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was my information that you were considering 92 bis rather than 92 ter. That -- we'll keep that in mind and we'll also look at how much time will be saved by that. We'll have a break until ten minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, in view of the latest information the Chamber received, we'll not insist on you speeding up. Of course the same is true for other Defence counsel. This at the same time is not an invitation to slow down unnecessarily. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, I want to just conclude the questions I was asking you, please, about the Serbian military offensive between 9th and 12th August, 1998, by suggesting to you that in consequence of that the KLA was driven out of the entire area around Gllogjan and did not even begin to return until sometime in the area of the 20th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to know what counsel means by the territory -- "the entire area around Gllogjan".

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me confine the question to Gllogjan itself for a moment, then. I want to suggest to you, Mr. Zlatkovic, that the KLA was driven out of Gllogjan in this offensive and that it was not for several weeks that reports began to reach Gjakove police station that they were beginning to return and re-organise?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible they were driven out of Glodjane, but they withdrew only as far as the Perimi [phoen] farm in Rznic and the canal, and they may have crossed the canal in the direction of Ratis. It's possible, but I wasn't there to see for myself whether they had been driven out of Glodjane or not, but it's a small difference, a few kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You know who Zarko Bacetic is?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Bajcetic, Zarko Bajcetic, yes, I do know. I know. The chief of the state security in Djakovica -- in fact, he was an advisor, he wasn't really the chief. Sreten Camovic was the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you aware that he has testified in this court that there were armed engagements between the Serbs and the KLA in the area to the east of the road including in the area around the canal itself between July and October 1998?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which road are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The main road. The area around the east of the main Peje to Gjakove road, including in the area around the canal where the bodies were found. Did you know that he had given that testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what Zarko Bajcetic said. I'm telling you what happened. He could have said anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For our assistance, could you give us date and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, can I check that, Your Honour. It -- the last part of the answer that I'm citing was the re-examination of Mr. Bajcetic by Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I'll try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I'll try to find it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn, please, to tab 34 in the bundle, in the brown bundle. I think you were shown this document shortly before you came to testify by Mr. Dutertre. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you can confirm that it is a document dated the 20th of August headed: "Official note," and that the legend at the top records it as being a note of the RDB based in Gjakove; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two things I want to ask you about, if I may. First of all, the very first entry, which obviously is some two weeks or so before the arrests of Bekim Kalamashi and Zenelj Alija that you refer to in your witness statement, can we be clear, were you, in fact, aware some two weeks before those arrest of allegations that there were remains in the canal?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: The state security most probably learned that through their collaborators.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question I was asking you was whether you were aware of it, Mr. Zlatkovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I only heard about it. There were rumours that those people were missing, and through various conversations we received some information that most probably they had been put somewhere. One story said that they had been buried at a cemetery and another one said that they had been thrown into Lake Radonjic, into the lake itself. Those were the things we heard from the people we talked to. It was most probably the state security that got this information through their collaborators, through their people, and they wrote an official note about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But just to be clear, this is referring specifically to the canal, isn't it, this entry?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: The state security got information that this was in the canal, but the people we talked to, some said they had been buried in Volujak, others said they had been buried somewhere near the cemetery in Jablanica. There were various stories going around, but it was only when we found them that we knew. The state security most probably had specific information they got through their collaborators, so they got this information in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I want to look now, if I may, at the state of the assessment of the KLA in this area at that time. Could you turn to page 2 in the B/C/S, also page 2 in the English, and can you please start with the sixth paragraph down, can you find a paragraph that begins: "We possess operational intelligence that a certain number of the most extreme members of the DTG ..." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: " ... most extreme members of the DTG are returning to their DTG centres, after the most recent operations to break them up and clear the terrain. Thus, according to our most recent intelligence, terrorist groups have returned to," and then there's a list of places which includes Gllogjan and Prilep, "where they are attempting to re-organise, establishing guards, et cetera." And then it goes on: "The secessionists are using their return for propaganda purposes, 'raising the morale' of the bandits with phrases like: 'The KLA is regaining its lost positions ... Capturing the temporarily occupied territories from the Serbian foe ...'" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the areas they are describing is not just Gllogjan and Prilep but Jablanica and Crmljane; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Moving on to the eastern side of Lake Radoniq?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. On the eastern side.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I want to suggest to you that the KLA was effectively routed in that early August operation and that Serb forces had control of this entire area up to and including Lake Radoniq from the main road right the way across?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I've got some problems as far as the time is concerned because the document says that they have returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's unclear in your question as to when this may have happened. So would you be -- please be very precise --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not only in relation to the 9th and to the 12th but also in relation to the 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think in the second line, it says: "Are returning," of that paragraph and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document might not be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perfectly translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Very -- might not be without confusion, and therefore we should not add to that but rather try to make matters more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the suggestion at its most narrow, Mr. Zlatkovic. There was a period of time after the 12th of August when Serb forces remained in control of Gllogjan and the area around the canal.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they had control or not. They had their check-points there. Those are check-points near the school in Rznic, another near another school - what was its name now? - near the Visnjarnik or cherry orchards, so that's where they were always fired on from. There was always information coming in that they had been wounded there. But what you say about Crmljane, the area of Crmljane, Rakovina was always under attack from Crmljane. There was a check-point in Rakovina, so almost always they were under attack. Several policemen were killed in Rakovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: When I went there to carry out an on-site investigation when a policeman was killed, I was in a Lada car with a red cross and it was fired on from the bushes, and fortunately I survived but I was going with the humanitarians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zlatkovic, just to be clear, you've answered the question that I put to you by saying: "I don't know whether they had control or not. They had their check-points there" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this question is always -- already been asked of the witness I don't know how many times the question is going to be put to him, and he said what he knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, I don't know what the next question would be, because Mr. Emmerson only referred to the earlier answer and has not put either the same or another question after that. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I just want to be clear. You said in answer to my question when I put to you that the Serb forces remained in control of Gllogjan and the area around the canal: "I do not know whether they had control or not." Now, just to be clear, is that the position, is that the state of your knowledge, you don't know one way or the other, Mr. Zlatkovic? Because if that is the position please tell us so clearly.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb forces had positioned a check-point in Prilep, and Prilep is 2 or 3 kilometres away from Lake Radonjic. The Serb forces also puts up a check-point by the school in Rznici, and that is also about a kilometre and a half away. That's what I know. I know nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means that Lake Radonjic was not touched. They did not arrive there until September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it turned out to be the same question and it's the same answer as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How long was the check-point in Irzniq there for after the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Right up until the operation that was carried out at the end of August and beginning of September, and then, once again, this was established. And when the terrorist groups returned, other policemen were killed there in 1999 and 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- in Prilep, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We're not --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Which means that they held control of that area, but the groups were there. I don't know how many of them there were --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: -- But there must have been some there since people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We're not concerned about 1999. You've told us that there was a police check-point in Irzniq between the 12th of August and the time when you arrived at the canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the check-point did exist in Prilep and Rznic, but it's one and a half kilometres away, perhaps even two kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, you were asked to repeat your answer not because there was anything wrong but just because the interpreters couldn't hear it, so there's no need to be irritated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, and was the --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was the Serbian check-point in Irzniq manned with people with heavy weapons? Was it a -- an armed check-point?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: It was an armed check-point with light weapons, and of course they had hand-grenades and perhaps even hand mortar, but certainly rifles, machine-guns, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Can I then come to the arrests on the 3rd of September in Kodralija of Bekim Kalamashi and Zenelj Alija. You say in your witness statement, this is paragraphs 49 onwards, that you were present throughout the interviewing process of those two men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: The interviews were conducting by people who knew the Albanian language. I just controlled what were -- what they said and I entered Zenelj Alija and Bekim Kalamashi's room. I would listen to what was being discussed, and I would guide the people in the interview to ask the questions, the proper questions. So I was present when both these people were interviewed, but not throughout, just from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Did -- were you present when they were brought into the police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Bekim Kalamashi was in his underwear when he was brought into the police station, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's not true?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: He certainly wasn't in his underwear. He was wearing a track-suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was he brought in with other men?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Zenelj Alija and some other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were any of them stripped naked to their underwear when they were brought in?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't see them being stripped at all. How could we interview them in underwear, without underwear? It's not civilised, it's not humane. Where would you ever see anything like that take place?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zlatkovic, I'm not going to comment on the evidence that we've heard in that regard already, but I do want to suggest to you that these men were beaten, beaten before they arrived at the police station and beaten whilst they were there.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Bekim Kalamashi is a small guy. I don't believe that he could have been beaten and he didn't have any injuries either, because I talked to him first because he was a young boy, a young man. So I just wanted to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was it your decision to assign Rade Vlahovic to the interview process?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Rade Vlahovic was an inspector at that time, and he knew Albanian. He knew it well because he lived in Donje Ratiste. So he spoke pure Albanian and could interpret for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did these men not speak Serbian, the two people being interviewed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Bekim Kalamashi didn't speak Serbian. Zenelj Alija knew a little Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you -- I'm looking at your witness statement at this point. Did you make notes of these interviews as they were taking place?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Ranko Markovic, Rade Vlahovic, and Zivojin Stankovic did, whereas I dealt with the matter on the basis of the notes that had been compiled and on the basis of what I had heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just look at the last sentence of paragraph 51, Mr. Zlatkovic, in your witness statement. Do you see that? And I ask you the question again: Did you take notes during the interview process of what was being said?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps there's just a mistake here in where it says I made notes. I processed the subject matter, whereas it is the other men, Rade Markovic, Ljubisa Novakovic, Zivojin Stankovic and the rest who made notes and on the basis of those notes I dealt with the case and sent it on to the prosecution. So that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the answer is you did not make notes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I dealt with the case, the crime report which I sent on to the prosecutor on the basis of their statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, it's a reasonably straightforward question. If your witness statement you have written the following words which you told us this morning were true, namely you read the statement and would give the same evidence on oath. "I took notes of the responses that were translated to me by them," that is by the police officers. My question is: Did you or did you not take notes of the responses of the men who were being interviewed as they were being translated to you, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not say specifically for this case that I took notes, and I state again that I dealt with the case with Rade Nikolic and another one with Goran Mitic, but on the basis of the notes that were taken by others. The notes exist in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You've seen some witness statements that are signed by Bekim Kalamashi and Zenelj Alija. Are those the notes that you're referring to or were there other notes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Those are the notes, they're statements, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so as each interview takes place, it's recorded in the form of a statement, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can I ask you this, please: You've been shown two statements signed by Bekim Kalamashi -- I'm sorry, it's two statements attributed to Bekim Kalamashi, one signed and one unsigned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock. From what I hear now I'm afraid that you would not finish in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour may be right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we leave that until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zlatkovic, we'll adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will continue tomorrow at 9.00 in -- Madam Registrar informed me, but it's the same courtroom. Yes. So we would like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.00, and we hope to conclude your testimony tomorrow morning. Madam Usher, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony you have given, nor about the testimony still to be given. So don't speak with anyone about it. That's my instruction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nobody to speak to here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, some people use telephones now and then, Mr. Zlatkovic, so therefore --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't worry, I won't, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good to hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Heaven forbid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, two small issues. First of all, you put that question again to the witness where the witness said it might be a translation problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- about taking notes. I observe, first of all, that taking notes or producing a written statement, there's a lot of matters in between. Sometimes you consistently take notes and make them a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes you write down a few things for yourself. Of course, I'm not going -- do not know where you were heading for, but notes is -- might easily lead to confusion, that's one. Second, the witness said it might be a translation error. I take it that you'll check that before we continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In respect of that answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in respect of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I would certainly have that checked in relation to the two sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the witness testified that he saw special police forces, KLA, but he didn't see any VJ persons on the BBC video. I hope that you'll understand that this Chamber is not equipped well enough to immediately see there in the distance we find the VJ --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- person. So therefore it's -- the video has been played not once and has a certain importance for the case --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to interpret the video properly --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you're invited to carefully review the tape and to draw our attention to the appearance of any VJ staff. And I am aware that the Chamber has received evidence that earlier sometimes vehicles that initially were perhaps green later on turned out to be blue, so therefore if you don't see them, that's not absolute evidence that they are not there --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but if you can clearly see them, the Chamber would like that you draw the attention of the Chamber to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is some assistance, I think, to be derived from the testimony of Colonel Crosland who viewed the video out of court and made some comments about the people that he saw on the videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I should review it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And of course Your Honour will see there's evidence on the videotape of shelling taking place on the village of Irzniq, shelling being one of the functions of the VJ artillery rather than the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But not -- I cannot say that I've never seen any shelling apart from exercised by VJ artillery so therefore. We'll then certainly look at Colonel Crosland's explanation. Perhaps that's just a suggestion. If you can clearly identify, perhaps it would not be a bad idea to put that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I indicate to Your Honour, on a completely unrelated matter, that we will be filing in the next two hours a response --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I’m aware that a, most likely, opposition to the videolink will be filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And also a very brief response to the Prosecution's objections concerning provisional release.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's understood. We'll read that as soon as possible. Mr. Dutertre, any other procedural matter at this moment? I do understand that most likely we'll run out of witnesses tomorrow halfway the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. It is very unlikely that the next witness be here. We're still waiting for written confirmation. I could give you additional explanations if we were in closed session, but I don't think he's going to come this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
